pairs.difference: A: the glass rim and side panels read as thin clear glass, the ice is cloudy and soft-edged, and the straw and liquid are glossy. Wet, clear and paper finishes are separated, though A's numbers sit just under the real range because the subject is smooth. B: the gold frame has soft, waxy scrolls with little metal sheen, so it reads as moulded yellow resin. The diagonal streaks on the mirror look painted on, and the wall and stone floor carry a fine mottled grain. On the eye B is the weaker material match, but only slightly.
pairs.fix: Make the frame polished gold metal: sharp narrow highlights on the scroll ridges and darker reflections in the recesses. Keep the wall plain and smooth, with no speckle.

pairs.difference: A: wood grain on the horse body is fine and follows the form, and the saddle is a soft satin leather that differs clearly from the wood. B: the green armour is one even satin coat with faint smeared streaks, the grey rings look dusty and airbrushed, and the floorboards have long streaky strokes. B's detail is twice A's, which is the direction the lessons run.
pairs.fix: Give the binocular body a pebbled matte rubber surface, with cleanly polished dark metal rings and glossy lenses. Keep the floor grain faint and fine, with no long streaks.

pairs.difference: A: the spider's abdomen and legs carry an even dusting of fine noise across a dark satin coat, with small sharp eye highlights. It looks like a grainy render rather than a clean painted surface. B: the fan paper is plain and quiet with crisp pleat lines, and the wooden ribs are smooth with no added marks, closer to the quiet real surfaces. The evidence is weak because both cards are simple.
pairs.fix: Remove the speckled grain from the spider's body. Use a smooth, clean semi-matte shell with one soft highlight on the abdomen.

pairs.difference: A: the bar is concrete with fine pitting, the stools are glossy, the glassware is thin, and the fruit has separate finishes, so materials differ within the scene. Its measurements are identical to p05 B, so it is the same card and I treat it the same way in both pairs. B: logs, shingles and stones are all thick rounded toy shapes with one soft finish. The red shingles read as moulded plastic, and the log end-rings and door planks are drawn large and decorative.
pairs.fix: Use thinner, irregular shingles with a dry matte surface. Make the wood grain fine and quiet, and the stone rough and dull, so that wood, roof and stone do not share one smooth finish.

pairs.difference: A: the card is densely worked, with hairline cracks in the stone pillars, grainy stipple on the path, and thin crisp iron with even satin edges. It has the highest detail in this pair, and those added surface marks are the kind generated cards pile on. B: this is the same pool-bar card as p04 A, with mixed finishes (pitted concrete, glossy stools, thin glass). Its texture is fine, though its concrete speckle is not fully clean.
pairs.fix: Remove the small cracks and stippling. Make the stone pillars smooth and softly worn, with simple broad planes, and the path plain.

pairs.difference: A: the spotlight barrel is satin dark metal with long, soft sheen bands along the curve, and the lenses are glossy, so the two finishes separate clearly. B: the pump body is flat orange paint with a soft blotchy grain. The grey chipped patches at the base look stuck on, the dial and counter are crisp fussy decals, and the desert has speckled painterly noise.
pairs.fix: Give the pump smooth enamel paint with a broad soft highlight, chrome trim with clear reflections, and no chipped patches. Keep the desert background clean, without speckle.

pairs.difference: A: the candy is smooth and waxy with a few pale sugar flecks and a broad soft highlight. It is simple and quiet, but below the real range on detail and with almost no gloss measured, so this call is not clean. B: water beads are scattered over the fruit and plate, the watermelon flesh is stippled, and the orange segments are sharply veined. It is a busy, uniformly wet surface where the crisp small marks act as decoration, which matches the lessons, and its detail is in the upper part of the range.
pairs.fix: Remove most of the water drops. Paint the fruit flesh with soft, simple tones and few fine marks, and give the rind and plate different levels of shine.

pairs.difference: A: the moon has soft pits and quiet tonal patches with a matte, cheese-like surface and very little fine noise, though its detail measures slightly below the real range. B: the brass is a uniform glossy lacquer from bell to loop, with gloss above the real range. The red cord is drawn in thick, crisp twisted strands with a dense tassel fringe, which is enlarged detail set against smooth metal.
pairs.fix: Make the brass darker in the reflections, with narrow bright streaks rather than an even lacquer. Draw the cord thinner, with a soft fibre surface and fewer strands.

pairs.difference: A: the velvet has a soft nap with darker folds at the tufting, the small gold buttons have sharp metal highlights, and the wooden legs are polished, so three materials separate clearly. B: the locker, door, vents and hinge area share one glossy orange moulded plastic. Sheet metal never reads, the vents are chunky pads, and only the ball and books change finish.
pairs.fix: Make the locker thin painted sheet metal: flat panels, sharp folded edges, narrow pressed vents, a light matte paint with small scuffs and a metal handle.

pairs.difference: A: the lamp has the same framing and finish as the real street lamp in the reference sheet, with clean dark satin metal, milky glass and a soft bulb. B: the orange roof and yellow walls are saturated flat colour with long smeared streaks for grain. The rope has crisp fibres and the seeds have sharp lines, so grain sharpness jumps between parts. Its numbers are within range, so this rests on the eye and the anchor match.
pairs.fix: Paint the wood as weathered matte planks with fine, quiet grain in natural colours, and give the rope and seeds the same soft level of detail.

pairs.difference: A: the shoes have crisp perforated mesh, many outlined panels and thick glossy laces, at the very top of the real range for detail and gloss. It is the busy, sharp small detail that generated cards add. However, the matte upper and shiny sole do mix finishes well. B: the wax is smooth, translucent and truthful, and the brass dish is simple, though detail measures below range. Confidence is low because the numbers lean the other way from the eye.
pairs.fix: Simplify the shoes: use fewer panels, a quiet soft mesh with barely visible holes, and thinner, matte laces.

pairs.difference: A: the lantern has satin black metal with soft rim highlights and clear glass with sharp narrow reflections, so matte and shiny are well separated. B: the pillow is covered with an even fine fabric-noise grain and smeared radial wrinkles, its edges are soft, it has almost no sheen, and gloss and fine texture fall below the real range. It reads as a blurry noisy render, not clean fabric.
pairs.fix: Make the pillow smooth stretch fabric with crisp seam lines, a few clean soft folds and one gentle sheen along the top curve, with no grain.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through surface marks that are added rather than observed, and through finishes that fail to separate. Typical marks are stipple and speckle on walls, stone and sand, hairline cracks, scattered water drops, fussy crisp decals and thick rope strands. Grain is often long smeared streaks or an even noise film. Single objects tend to sit in one finish, such as moulded plastic on the locker and cabin, or uniform lacquer on the brass and resin-like gold. Real cards stay quieter and softer, with fine wood grain, simple planes, and sharp highlights only where the material is truly shiny. The measurements did not always agree with the eye: very smooth subjects (drink, candy, moon, candle) fall below the real range, so those calls are low confidence.
